provenance.instrument: East Donegal Township Zoning Ordinance (Chapter 52 Zoning, Ord. No. 2001-1, as amended), as published on Municode
provenance.status_detail: Municode Library, East Donegal Township, Lancaster County (the Village Center District is Maytown, 52-118(a)). District use lists and lot, yard and height tables are text in Article V. Floodplain rules are in Chapter 14, Floodplain Management. The Municode Ordinances tab lists 0 uncodified ordinances
provenance.code_current_through_note: Municode version 'May 8, 2025 (Current)': 'Codified through Ordinance No. 2025-1, enacted January 6, 2025. (Supp. No. 5)'. Article V history notes run through Ord. No. 2024-3 of 5-2-2024. Municode lists no uncodified ordinances
checks: Elder cottage: 'a small manufactured or modular, free-standing housing unit specifically designed for elderly disabled or handicapped persons', designed to be moved and installed on the same lot as an existing principal dwelling (52-27). A conditional use from the Board of Supervisors in A, R-2, R-3 and R-4 (52-114(b)(2)j, 52-116(b)(2)c, 52-117(b)(2)d, 52-118(b)(2)b). C, R-1, R-5, GC, PC and I do not list it. AC lists 'Dwelling units' as a use by right (52-123(b)(1)j)

Elder cottage standards: one per lot, at most 900 sq ft of floor area, combined lot coverage within the district maximum, occupied by an elderly (60 or over), handicapped or disabled person related to the occupants of the house by blood, marriage or adoption, at most two people, connected to the house's utilities with no separate systems, one parking space beyond the house's, only to the side or rear of the house and within the side and rear yard setbacks, a site plan, an affidavit that the owner of the house lives in one of the two units and that the cottage is removed within 90 days after it is no longer used by a qualifying person, and a temporary use and occupancy certificate renewed every 12 months (52-268(1) to (11)). In the conditional use process the Board of Supervisors may modify or waive any of these specific criteria (52-249(b))

Residential conversion of an existing building into more units: a conditional use in R-3 and R-4. At least 800 sq ft per unit, 3,000 sq ft of lot area per unit plus 500 sq ft per added bedroom, a building that existed before the chapter, no extension or outside change except for access or safety, frontage on a public street and rear frontage on an alley, public sewer and water, parking behind the front building line (52-117(b)(2)a, 52-118(b)(2)a, 52-291)

More than one principal structure: 'more than one structure housing a permitted or permissible principal use may be erected on a single lot, provided that yard and other requirements of this chapter shall be met for each structure as though it were on an individual lot' (52-149). Read with the lot area among the other requirements, the lot needs the district lot area for each dwelling. In C and A the number of uses and lots from a 1975 tract is limited (52-113(c)(1), 52-114(c)(1))

A permits single-family semi-detached dwellings, R-3 and R-4 semi-detached dwellings, R-4 and R-5 townhouses, and R-5 multifamily dwellings, each as new buildings (52-114(b)(1)i, 52-117(b)(1)b, 52-118(b)(1), 52-119(b)(1))

Manufactured home for agricultural uses: a special exception in A for one manufactured home per farm, permanently occupied by someone who works at least 240 hours a year on the farm, set back 100 ft from the street, 12 ft from side lines and 25 ft from rear lines (52-114(b)(3)c, 52-277)

Adaptive reuse of a historic resource on the historic resource map: a conditional use in all districts for a mix of residential and nonresidential uses, including multifamily dwellings, on a lot of two acres or more (52-124(o))

Front yards depend on the street class. In C, A and R-1 on a local street 60 ft from the centerline or 35 ft from the right-of-way, whichever is greater, and more on collector and arterial streets. In R-2 and R-3 50 ft from the centerline or 25 ft from the right-of-way on arterial, collector and local streets alike, and more only on PA Route 441. In R-4 on a local street 25 ft from the centerline or 10 ft from the right-of-way, on a collector 25 ft or 10 ft, and on an arterial 50 ft or 25 ft (52-113(d) to 52-118(d))

Accessory buildings meet the front yard of the house and, 'In all other instances', stand at least 10 ft from side and rear lines (2 and 3 ft for rear-yard garages in the Village Center District), and together may cover at most 25% of the required rear yard (52-147(a), (d)). Accessory buildings may be 30 ft tall in C and A, 25 ft in R-1 to R-5
R-1, R-2, R-3 and R-4: no dwelling unit within 50 ft of land in the Agricultural District (52-115(d)(3), 52-116(d)(3), 52-117(d)(3), 52-118(d)(3))

Floodplain (Chapter 14): any new construction or substantial improvement in the identified floodplain is prohibited unless a variance is granted, manufactured homes are prohibited there unless a variance is granted, and no new construction or development within 50 ft landward of the top of bank of any watercourse in the floodplain (14-124(d), 14-125, 14-129(a)). Substantial improvement is work of 50% or more of the market value (14-36)

A use neither permitted nor denied is prohibited unless the Zoning Hearing Board finds by special exception that it is of the same general character as the district's permitted uses (52-62). AC lists dwelling units, so the unlisted-use path is not read to reach it. A nonconforming lot may be used for any use permitted in its district if yards, height and open space are met (52-89(a))

Parking: two off-street spaces per dwelling unit, paved and all-weather. 'Space within a private garage or within a garage incorporated within a dwelling shall not be considered a parking space' (52-182(a), 52-183(a), (c))
A dwelling unit with an industrial use, for an owner or caretaker, is a conditional use in I on a lot of two acres or more (52-267). It is not a unit added to a house
Variances: the Zoning Hearing Board on the findings of 52-352(a)(1) to (6). No bar on a use variance was found
provenance.notes: Read in a browser on Municode on 2026-11-17, one page at a time, by text and screenshots. Read: Article V (52-113 to 52-119 in full, the use lists of 52-120 to 52-122, 52-124(o)), Article IV, 52-61, 52-62, 52-147, 52-149, 52-150, 52-183, 52-267, 52-268, 52-277, 52-291, parts of 52-27 (dwelling types, elder cottage, elderly, lot coverage) and Chapter 14 to 14-125. Not read: R-4 setbacks after 52-118(c)(5), 52-120 to 52-123 lot figures, the AC use list, the rest of 52-124, 52-148, 52-151 to 52-156, 52-181, 52-182, 52-184 to 52-187, Article VIII, the rest of Article IX, Articles X to XIII (including the variance section 52-352 and conditional use procedure 52-354), most of 52-27 (family not found), Chapter 14 after 14-125 and Chapter 42 (subdivision and land development). A later check read 52-27 'Family', 'Residential floor area' and 'Single-family detached dwelling', 52-118(d), 52-123(b)(1), 52-182, 52-183(c), 52-249(b), 52-267, 52-352, and Chapter 14 sections 14-36, 14-129 and 14-188, and the Municode code page.

term.note: 'a small manufactured or modular, free-standing housing unit specifically designed for elderly disabled or handicapped persons. This unit is designed to be transported and moved and to be installed on the same lot as an existing principal dwelling'

status.note: A conditional use from the Board of Supervisors. Only an elderly, handicapped or disabled relative of the occupants of the house

scope_districts.note: Elder cottage is a listed conditional use in these four districts

status_outside.note: C, R-1, R-5, GC, PC and I do not list an elder cottage. AC lists 'Dwelling units' by right (52-123(b)(1)j) but no elder cottage, and its list was not read in full

path.note: 'Within a zoning district in which an elder cottage is permitted by conditional use, the board of supervisors may approve such a use'. The Board may modify or waive any of the specific criteria during the conditional use process (52-249(b))

fallback_path.note: Zoning Hearing Board on the findings of 52-352(a)(1) to (6). No bar on a use variance was found

unlisted_use_path.note: 'Where a use is neither specifically permitted nor denied, it shall be assumed to be prohibited, unless and until approved by the zoning hearing board'

unlisted_use_scope.quote: the proposed use shall be of the same general character as the uses permitted in the specific zoning district
unlisted_use_scope.note: The elder cottage is listed in other districts, so whether it is 'neither specifically permitted nor denied' in these districts is not settled

unlisted_use_districts.note: AC is left out: it lists 'Dwelling units' as a use by right (52-123(b)(1)j), so a dwelling there is not a use neither permitted nor denied

value.name: Residential conversion (R-3, R-4)
value.conditions: An existing building converted into more dwelling units. Each unit at least 800 sq ft, 3,000 sq ft of lot area per unit plus 500 sq ft for each added bedroom, district yards not reduced, no extension or outside change except for access or safety, frontage on a public street and rear frontage on an alley, public sewer and water, and parking behind the front building line

requires.condition: The building existed before the date of the ordinance from which the chapter is derived
The lot has rear yard frontage on an alley

value.note: A building divided into units, not a unit added to a house

value.name: Second principal dwelling on the lot
value.conditions: More than one structure housing a permitted principal use may stand on a lot if 'yard and other requirements of this chapter shall be met for each structure as though it were on an individual lot'. In C, A and AC the number of uses from a tract of record in 1975 is limited
value.note: A second house, not an accessory unit. The lot figures are twice the district minimum, on the reading that the lot area is one of the 'other requirements'. The C, R-1, R-5 and AC minimums are not on file. Whether a land development plan is needed under Chapter 42 was not settled

requires.condition: Each dwelling meets the district lot area, yards and other requirements as though it were on its own lot

value.name: Manufactured home for agricultural uses (A)
value.conditions: An accessory use to an agricultural operation, one per farm, permanently occupied by at least one person who works at least 240 hours a year on the farm, set back 100 ft from any street right-of-way, 12 ft from side lines and 25 ft from rear lines, with approved water and sewage. The use and occupancy certificate is renewed every year and the home is removed within 30 days if the occupancy rule is not met

requires.condition: The lot is a farm in agricultural operation and the occupant works on it

value.note: Housing for farm workers on a farm, not a general ADU

building_types.note: 'on the lot of a principal dwelling'. No house type is named

value.condition: The cottage must be physically connected to the water, sewage and other utilities serving the house, with no separate systems. With on-site sewer or water the applicant must show the systems can serve both units.

Before the use and occupancy permit, an affidavit that the occupant of the house will live in the house or the cottage while both exist, and that the cottage will be removed within 90 days after it is no longer occupied by a qualifying person. The certificate is temporary and reviewed every 12 months for a fee.

The total lot coverage of the house, existing accessory structures and the cottage may not exceed the district maximum. In A the number of uses and lots from a lot of record on January 8, 1975 is limited, and whether the cottage counts as an added use is not settled.
No dwelling unit may stand within 50 ft of land in the Agricultural District.

Within any identified floodplain area 'any new construction or substantial improvements shall be prohibited', and manufactured homes are prohibited there, each unless a variance is obtained under Article VIII of Chapter 14. An elder cottage is a manufactured or modular unit. No new construction may stand within 50 ft landward of the top of bank of any watercourse.

types_allowed.note: A 'small manufactured or modular, free-standing housing unit' placed to the side or rear of the house

types_not_addressed.note: The code names only a free-standing manufactured or modular unit

value.detached_new: free-standing manufactured or modular elder cottage

max_sqft.note: 'The elder cottage may not exceed 900 square feet of floor area.'

family_only.note: The occupant is an elderly, handicapped or disabled person related to the occupants of the house. 'Family' (52-27) is people related by blood, marriage or adoption, including foster care, up to three unrelated people, or the residents of a licensed group home

occupancy.value: An elderly (60 or over), handicapped or disabled person related to the occupants of the house by blood, marriage or adoption, and at most two people. The cottage is removed within 90 days after no qualifying person lives in it.

owner_occupancy.note: The occupant of the house must live in the house or the cottage. No rule that this person owns the lot was found

max_adus.note: 'No more than one elder cottage shall be permitted on the lot of a principal dwelling.'

front_yard_barred.note: 'The elder cottage shall be installed and located only to the side or rear of the principal dwelling'

district_yards_bind_accessory.note: 'and shall adhere to all side and rear yard setback requirements'. 52-268(8) does not say whether these are the principal building's yards or the accessory building yards of 52-147(a), at least 10 ft from side and rear lines. The larger of the two is shown

accessory_cap_binds_adu.note: Whether the accessory building height of the district reaches an elder cottage is not settled. 52-268 sets no height

spaces_required.note: 'A minimum of one all-weather off-street parking space, with unrestricted ingress and egress to the street, shall be provided for the elder cottage, in addition to that required for the principal dwelling'

total_on_site.note: Two for the house and one for the cottage. Space in a private garage does not count as a parking space (52-183(c))

reading.value: 52-183(a) asks two spaces for every dwelling unit, so a reading that counts the cottage as a dwelling unit gives two for it and four in all

min_lot_sqft.note: Single-family dwelling units. A new residential lot from a tract may be at most two acres (52-114(c)(1)e)

setback_front_ft.note: On a local access street 60 ft from the centerline or 35 ft from the right-of-way, whichever is greater. More on collector and arterial streets

max_impervious_coverage.note: 'Max. Lot Coverage'. Lot coverage is the ratio of all impervious surfaces to the lot area

min_lot_sqft.note: Public sewer and water are required (52-116(c)(3))

setback_front_ft.note: 50 ft from the centerline or 25 ft from the right-of-way, whichever is greater, on arterial, collector and local streets. More only on PA Route 441

min_lot_sqft.note: Single-family detached. Public sewer and water are required (52-117(c)(3))

setback_front_ft.note: 50 ft from the centerline or 25 ft from the right-of-way, whichever is greater, on arterial, collector and local streets. More only on PA Route 441

min_lot_sqft.note: Single-family detached. Lots at least 250 ft deep, fronting a public street and reaching an alley or another street

setback_front_ft.note: Local access: '25 feet from the centerline of the existing or proposed street or ten feet from the edge of the existing or proposed right-of-way, whichever is the greater'. The centerline figure may govern. Collectors 25 ft from the centerline or 10 ft from the right-of-way, arterials 50 ft or 25 ft

accessory_setback_side_ft.note: An accessory building stands at least 10 ft from side lines. The R-4 principal side yard is 3 ft, and 52-268(8) does not say which side yard binds the cottage, so the larger is shown
